title: Explicit negation: session store does NOT use Redis
notes: Tests meaning-reversal resistance: the session mentions Redis by name only to explicitly rule it out. A good extractor must capture the NEGATIVE fact (no Redis) rather than dropping the negation and recording the positive-polarity opposite (Redis IS used) — the worst class of extraction failure per FEAT-542.

turns.text: Quick heads up on caching — we are NOT using Redis for the session store, in case that assumption is baked into anyone's mental model.
Good to know. So no Redis dependency for sessions at all — what are we using instead?
Plain in-process LRU cache for now. It's simpler and we don't have multi-instance session sharing yet.
Got it — in-process LRU cache, no Redis, no cross-instance sharing. I'll keep that in mind.

gold_atoms.text: The session store does NOT use Redis — it uses a plain in-process LRU cache instead.
There is no multi-instance session sharing yet, a consequence of the in-process cache choice.

forbidden_items: The session store uses Redis for session storage
